BCI-NAOH-SOL.note: Same NaOH chemistry as two commercial forms, not two products. Liquid is the standard bulk-buyer form; flake/solid is chosen specifically for remote/freeze-risk locations where shipping water is uneconomical (see supplier note).

varRows.s: Bagged solid · avoids shipping water weight, higher energy cost to produce

BCI-ALUM-LIQ.note: Same aluminum sulfate chemistry — liquid is the standard form for continuous-dosing municipal water treatment; granular is used where dry storage/dosing is preferred.

varRows.s: Dry storage/dosing · higher processing cost per unit active

BCI-FE2SO4-LIQ.note: Same ferric sulfate chemistry — liquid is standard for continuous municipal dosing; granular for dry-storage applications.

BCI-FESO4-HEP.note: Same ferrous sulfate chemistry at different hydration states. Heptahydrate (~55% FeSO4) is the more common commercial form; monohydrate (~90-94% FeSO4) is more concentrated per unit weight but costs more to produce.

SUR-AES-2EO.note: Same SLES chemistry at different ethoxylation degrees. 2EO is the more common personal-care default; 3EO uses more ethylene oxide per mole and typically costs slightly more.

varRows.s: Higher ethoxylation — more EO input per mole

SUR-SLS-PST.note: Same SLS chemistry — paste is the standard bulk liquid form; powder/needle requires spray-drying, adding real processing cost.

varRows.s: Spray-dried · higher processing cost, easier to ship (less water)

PFC-H2O2-35.note: Same H2O2 chemistry — concentration is a dilution/shipping choice for industrial grades, while electronic grade is a fundamentally different ultra-high-purity specification (not just concentration), commanding a dramatically higher price for semiconductor wafer cleaning.

varRows.s: More concentrated — less water shipped per unit active
Ultra-high-purity, semiconductor wafer cleaning — different specification tier entirely, not just concentration

SIL-EMU-35.note: Same silicone emulsion chemistry at different concentrations for different end uses — 35% is the personal-care dilution, 60% the more concentrated industrial grade.

SIL-PDMS-LOW.note: Same PDMS chemistry at different molecular weights/viscosity grades — low viscosity is the more commodity, broadly-used grade; high viscosity (higher polymerization) is the elastomer/gum-base tier.

CLN-CA-PWD.note: Same citric acid chemistry — cleaning grade is the lower-certification base; food grade requires FCC/USP-level purity and certification, commanding a real premium.

OLE-GLY-CRD.note: Same glycerine chemistry — crude is the raw biodiesel/oleochemical co-product; refined requires significant purification for food/pharma/personal-care use, a real and growing cost step as more Indonesian operators add on-site purification (see supplier note).

FOD-LEC-LIQ.note: Same lecithin chemistry — liquid is the standard bulk form; de-oiled powder requires additional fractionation/deoiling processing for dry-mix and high-phosphatidylcholine applications.

ADV-CF-TOW.note: Carbon fibre is sold by tow count (thousands of filaments per tow — 1K to 48K), not by region-specific grade. Larger tows (24K/48K) cost less per kg but are harder to weave into fine fabrics; 12K is the standard industrial default. Region below reflects where the fibre is produced/priced, independent of tow count.

varRows.s: Fine weave, sporting goods, premium automotive
Industrial standard default — best balance of cost and processability
Lower cost per kg, coarser weave, wind energy/infrastructure
Lowest cost per kg, industrial/structural use only
